executive_summary.text: A critical SQL injection flaw in Ghost CMS (CVE-2026-26980, CVSS 9.4) has been actively exploited to compromise 700+ websites — including domains tied to Harvard, Oxford, and DuckDuckGo — turning them into ClickFix social-engineering launchpads that trick visitors into executing malicious PowerShell commands.

The Laravel-Lang PHP package ecosystem was poisoned in a coordinated supply chain attack where malicious version tags — published within a 15-minute window — introduced backdoors designed to exfiltrate CI/CD secrets and deliver a cross-platform credential-stealing payload.

The FBI issued an alert for Kali365, a phishing-as-a-service platform that weaponizes OAuth device code authentication flows to steal Microsoft 365 session tokens and bypass MFA — lowering the technical barrier for account takeover attacks against business tenants.

Supply chain attacks reached epidemic scale this week: the 'Megalodon' campaign infected 5,500+ GitHub repositories via fake automated commits injecting credential-harvesting Actions workflows, while the 'TrapDoor' campaign simultaneously spread infostealers across npm, PyPI, and Crates.io.

North Korea's Lazarus Group has deployed RemotePE, a memory-resident, fileless RAT that loads entirely from DPAPI-encrypted blobs into process memory — leaving no on-disk artifacts — as part of a multi-stage campaign targeting financial and cryptocurrency organizations.

cyber_news.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploited to Hijack 700+ Sites for ClickFix Attacks
cyber_news.summary: Threat actors are mass-exploiting a critical SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-26980, CVSS 9.4) in Ghost CMS's unauthenticated Content API, injecting malicious JavaScript into compromised sites to deliver ClickFix social-engineering lures. Over 700 websites have been confirmed affected, including high-trust domains associated with Harvard, Oxford, and DuckDuckGo. Researchers at QiAnXin XLab attribute the activity to a coordinated, opportunistic threat cluster scanning for exposed Ghost instances.
cyber_news.expanded: CVE-2026-26980 is an unauthenticated SQL injection in Ghost CMS's Content API endpoint, allowing attackers to read arbitrary data from the backend database without any credentials. Once initial access is achieved, attackers inject a malicious JavaScript snippet into site content or themes that renders a fake browser verification dialog — the 'ClickFix' technique — which instructs visitors to paste and run a PowerShell command, typically resulting in infostealer or RAT deployment on visitor endpoints. The high-trust reputation of compromised domains (university and well-known tech sites) significantly increases the probability that targets will comply with the fake prompt. The exploitation timeline is rapid: mass scanning for vulnerable Ghost instances appears to have begun within days of the CVE's public disclosure, making unpatched deployments extremely high-risk.

cyber_news.title: Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised to Deliver Cross-Platform Credential Stealer
cyber_news.summary: Attackers hijacked the Laravel-Lang localization packages on GitHub, publishing malicious version tags within a 15-minute burst to introduce backdoored code targeting CI/CD pipelines and developer workstations. The malicious payloads are designed to exfiltrate CI secrets, API keys, and credentials, and deploy a cross-platform infostealer capable of running on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Any PHP/Laravel project consuming affected package versions via Composer is potentially impacted.
cyber_news.expanded: The attack abused GitHub's tag-based release mechanism: by creating new semver-compatible tags pointing to poisoned commits, the attackers ensured that Composer dependency resolution would pull the backdoored code for projects with loose version constraints. The malicious code introduced a backdoor that reached out to attacker-controlled infrastructure to exfiltrate environment variables — prime targets include API tokens, database credentials, cloud provider secrets (AWS_ACCESS_KEY, etc.), and CI runner tokens. The 15-minute publication window suggests coordinated account access, possibly through a previously stolen maintainer credential or OAuth token. Because Composer caches package metadata, projects that resolved dependencies during the window may have cached the malicious version without subsequent pulls being affected, complicating incident response.

cyber_news.title: FBI Warns of Kali365 PhaaS Targeting Microsoft 365 via OAuth Device Code Abuse
cyber_news.summary: The FBI has issued a formal warning about Kali365, a phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platform that enables low-skill attackers to conduct Microsoft 365 account takeovers by abusing the OAuth device code authentication flow to capture session tokens and circumvent MFA. The platform is being marketed on criminal forums and significantly lowers the technical entry point for M365-focused attacks. Both enterprise and SMB tenants are considered at risk.
cyber_news.expanded: OAuth device code flow abuse works by generating a legitimate Microsoft device authentication code, then socially engineering the target into entering it at the real Microsoft login page — meaning no phishing infrastructure needs to proxy or intercept credentials directly. Once the victim authenticates, the attacker receives a valid access token and refresh token for the account, granting persistent access that survives password resets unless the token is explicitly revoked. Kali365 automates this entire flow with a turnkey UI, pre-built lure templates, and token management dashboards, making it operationally equivalent to traditional adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) kits but without requiring a proxy server. Conditional Access Policies that restrict device code flow are the primary technical control to block this attack class.

cyber_news.title: Over 5,500 GitHub Repositories Infected in 'Megalodon' Supply Chain Attack
cyber_news.summary: A supply chain campaign dubbed 'Megalodon' has infected more than 5,500 GitHub repositories by injecting malicious GitHub Actions workflows via fake automated commits, targeting CI/CD credentials, secrets, API keys, and tokens stored in runner environments. The scale of the campaign makes it one of the largest known GitHub-focused supply chain operations on record. Downstream consumers of affected repositories may have executed malicious workflows without awareness.
cyber_news.expanded: Megalodon operates by gaining write access to repositories — likely through compromised maintainer accounts or tokens harvested from earlier supply chain incidents — and committing workflow YAML files that appear to be routine dependency updates or bot-generated housekeeping commits. The injected Actions workflows execute on GitHub's hosted runners, where they enumerate and exfiltrate environment secrets, repository secrets, and any credentials cached in the runner context. Critically, forks and projects that pin to a branch (rather than a commit hash) may automatically pull and execute the malicious workflow on their next CI run. The attackers appear to be aggregating harvested secrets into a central collection infrastructure for downstream monetization or credential stuffing.

cyber_news.title: TrapDoor Supply Chain Attack Spreads Credential-Stealing Malware via npm, PyPI, and Crates.io
cyber_news.summary: A coordinated cross-ecosystem supply chain campaign named 'TrapDoor' has planted credential-stealing malware packages across npm, PyPI, and Crates.io simultaneously, targeting developers across the JavaScript, Python, and Rust ecosystems. The campaign leverages typosquatting, dependency confusion, and compromised maintainer accounts to distribute infostealers that harvest credentials, browser-stored passwords, and environment variables. The cross-ecosystem nature of the attack suggests a well-resourced and organized threat actor.
cyber_news.expanded: TrapDoor packages are designed to blend in as legitimate utility or helper libraries, using naming patterns that closely mimic popular packages to maximize install rates through both human error (typosquatting) and automated dependency resolution (dependency confusion). Upon installation, the malicious packages execute setup scripts or install hooks that run a payload retrieval stager, downloading the primary infostealer from attacker-controlled CDN infrastructure to evade static package scanning. The stealer component targets browser credential stores (Chrome, Firefox, Edge), SSH key files, .env files, and shell history — effectively turning a developer workstation compromise into a pivot point for accessing every system the developer has credentials for. The simultaneous cross-registry deployment indicates either a single actor with broad reach or a coordinated group sharing tooling.

cyber_news.title: Lazarus Group Deploys RemotePE Memory-Only RAT Against Financial and Crypto Firms
cyber_news.summary: North Korea's Lazarus Group has been observed using RemotePE, a novel cross-platform remote access trojan that operates entirely in memory without writing artifacts to disk, as part of a multi-stage attack campaign against financial institutions and cryptocurrency organizations. The malware is loaded via a two-stage loader chain (DPAPILoader → RemotePELoader) that decrypts and injects the RAT payload directly into process memory using Windows DPAPI for key storage. Fox-IT researchers attributed the activity to Lazarus with high confidence.
cyber_news.expanded: The attack chain begins with DPAPILoader, which retrieves an encrypted blob stored in the Windows Data Protection API (DPAPI) credential store — a location that requires user-context access to decrypt, effectively tying the payload to the compromised user account and complicating cross-system analysis. DPAPILoader passes the decrypted PE blob to RemotePELoader, which performs reflective PE injection to load RemotePE directly into a legitimate host process's memory space. Because RemotePE never touches disk, traditional file-based AV and EDR signatures are ineffective; detection requires behavioral analysis of in-memory PE anomalies, abnormal DPAPI access patterns, or network-layer C2 traffic analysis. The targeting of financial and crypto firms aligns with Lazarus's well-documented objective of generating revenue for the North Korean state through cyber theft.

cyber_news.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Zero-Day Exploited to Deploy Godzilla Webshell and Cobalt Strike
cyber_news.summary: A zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-5426, CVSS 7.5) in the KnowledgeDeliver Learning Management System — popular among Japanese organizations — was exploited in the wild to deliver the Godzilla web shell and subsequently deploy Cobalt Strike Beacon for persistent command-and-control. The flaw stems from hard-coded ASP.NET machine keys, allowing attackers to forge ViewState payloads and achieve remote code execution. The vulnerability has since been patched, but exploitation preceded disclosure.
cyber_news.expanded: The root cause — hard-coded ASP.NET machine keys — is a well-understood but persistently recurring vulnerability class. ASP.NET uses machine keys to cryptographically sign and optionally encrypt ViewState, a serialized object passed between client and server. When the machine key is known (whether hard-coded, leaked, or sourced from public repositories), an attacker can craft a malicious serialized ViewState payload containing a deserialization gadget chain that executes arbitrary code on the server when the application processes it. The Godzilla web shell is a sophisticated, encrypted, Java/ASP.NET-compatible shell that communicates over standard HTTP with encrypted request/response payloads, evading many WAF signatures. Once established, the attackers used Godzilla as a staging point to deploy Cobalt Strike Beacon for full C2 capability, lateral movement, and likely ransomware or data exfiltration follow-through.

cyber_news.title: 'Underminr' Vulnerability Lets Attackers Disguise C2 Traffic Behind Trusted Domains
cyber_news.summary: A newly disclosed vulnerability class dubbed 'Underminr' affects approximately 88 million domains and allows attackers to route malicious connections — including command-and-control traffic — through infrastructure associated with trusted, allowlisted domains, effectively bypassing DNS filtering, web proxies, and security controls that rely on domain reputation. The technique exploits delegation and redirect behaviors in DNS and HTTP that are broadly trusted by network security tooling. No single CVE has been assigned as the issue is systemic across many platforms.
cyber_news.expanded: Underminr abuses legitimate subdomain delegation and HTTP redirect chains that exist on widely-trusted domains (CDNs, SaaS platforms, cloud providers) to act as transparent relays for attacker-controlled endpoints. Because the initial DNS query resolves to a reputable IP space and the TLS certificate belongs to the trusted provider, security controls that evaluate traffic at the domain or IP level grant implicit approval. The technique is particularly effective against DNS-based filtering solutions (Cisco Umbrella, Cloudflare Gateway, etc.) that do not perform full content inspection of proxied or redirected traffic. Threat actors can leverage this to establish C2 channels that appear to be legitimate traffic to cloud services, making behavioral detection dependent on anomalous data volume patterns or endpoint-level telemetry rather than network-layer controls.

cyber_news.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 Operators Providing Infrastructure for Russian Cyberattacks
cyber_news.summary: Dutch authorities have seized 800 servers and arrested two co-owners of hosting companies accused of providing bulletproof IT infrastructure used by Russian state-linked actors to conduct cyberattacks, influence operations, and disinformation campaigns inside the EU. The hosting entities had assumed control over infrastructure previously associated with Stark Industries Solutions, a provider sanctioned by the EU for its role in Russian offensive cyber operations. The action is one of the largest infrastructure seizures targeting Russian cyber-enabler networks.
cyber_news.expanded: The arrested operators ran hosting companies that served as a technical and legal buffer between Russian cyber operatives and the infrastructure they depended on — a classic bulletproof hosting model where abuse complaints are ignored and law enforcement requests stonewalled. By taking over the Stark Industries Solutions infrastructure network, the operators gave sanctioned Russian cyber actors continued access to IP space and server resources under a nominally cleaner corporate identity. The 800-server seizure disrupts active C2 infrastructure, botnet nodes, and likely credential-harvesting servers across multiple ongoing campaigns. This operation follows a pattern of Western law enforcement increasingly targeting the hosting ecosystem that enables state-sponsored cyber operations, recognizing that disrupting infrastructure has more immediate operational impact than indictments alone.

cyber_news.title: npm Adds 2FA-Gated Publishing and Package Install Controls to Combat Supply Chain Attacks
cyber_news.summary: GitHub has rolled out new npm registry security controls requiring maintainers to approve package releases via 2FA-gated workflows before packages become publicly available, alongside new package install controls that allow organizations to restrict which packages can be pulled by their projects. The changes directly address the account-takeover and unauthorized-publish attack vectors that have enabled numerous supply chain compromises. Adoption is opt-in for existing packages but enforced for new high-impact packages.
cyber_news.expanded: The 2FA-gated publishing mechanism introduces a cryptographic approval step where a release cannot be published until a maintainer with 2FA-enabled credentials explicitly signs off on the specific version — preventing scenarios where a stolen session token or API key alone is sufficient to push malicious code. The package install controls work as an allowlist mechanism at the organization or project level, blocking dependency resolution from pulling packages that haven't been explicitly approved, which directly counters dependency confusion attacks. These controls are architecturally significant because they shift npm's security model from reactive (flagging malicious packages after publication) to preventive (blocking unauthorized publication and consumption). MSPs managing development environments should evaluate enforcing these controls across client development toolchains.

cyber_news.title: Packagist Supply Chain Attack Backdoors 8 PHP Packages with GitHub-Hosted Linux Malware
cyber_news.summary: A coordinated supply chain attack has compromised eight packages on Packagist, the primary PHP package repository, injecting malicious code that downloads and executes a Linux binary hosted on GitHub Releases infrastructure. The attack targets Linux-based PHP application servers, consistent with production web hosting environments. The use of GitHub Releases as a payload delivery mechanism leverages GitHub's trusted infrastructure to bypass domain-based security controls.
cyber_news.expanded: By hosting the malicious Linux binary on GitHub Releases rather than on attacker-owned infrastructure, the attackers exploit GitHub's IP reputation and TLS certificate to bypass firewall rules and proxy controls that would block connections to unknown external domains. The injected PHP code acts as a dropper: it retrieves the binary at package install or runtime, writes it to a temporary location, makes it executable, and runs it — a pattern that evades many static package scanning tools focused on PHP code analysis rather than download behavior. The binary payload's capabilities have not been fully disclosed, but given the pattern across concurrent campaigns this week, credential theft and persistent backdoor functionality are likely objectives. Affected Packagist packages span multiple functional categories, suggesting maintainer account compromise rather than a single targeted vendor.

deep_dive.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980: Mass Exploitation Turns 700+ Trusted Websites into ClickFix Attack Platforms
deep_dive.content: CVE-2026-26980 is a critical unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability (CVSS 9.4) in Ghost CMS's Content API, exploitable without any credentials or user interaction. Threat actors — tracked by QiAnXin XLab as an opportunistic but technically capable cluster — began mass-scanning for exposed Ghost instances within days of disclosure, ultimately compromising over 700 sites including domains associated with Harvard University, Oxford University, and DuckDuckGo. The attack chain works in two stages: first, the SQL injection is used to read arbitrary data from the Ghost database (potentially including admin credentials, API keys, and content), and second, attackers inject malicious JavaScript into site themes or content that renders fake browser or CAPTCHA verification dialogs consistent with the 'ClickFix' social engineering technique. When site visitors encounter these dialogs, they are prompted to open a Run dialog and paste a provided command — typically a PowerShell one-liner that downloads and executes an infostealer or remote access trojan. The high-reputation nature of compromised domains dramatically increases visitor trust in the fake prompts. The attack weaponizes legitimate infrastructure rather than standalone phishing pages, making URL-based blocking largely ineffective. All Ghost CMS deployments should be treated as compromised and patched immediately, with post-compromise review of injected content and downstream visitor notification considered for confirmed victims.

biggest_hacks.title: 7-Eleven Data Breach Exposes Personal Information of 185,000 People
biggest_hacks.summary: The ShinyHunters extortion gang breached 7-Eleven's systems in April 2026, stealing personal information belonging to over 183,000 individuals, with the data subsequently surfacing on Have I Been Pwned.

biggest_hacks.title: 266,000 Affected by Data Breach at Radiology Associates of Richmond
biggest_hacks.summary: Threat actors exfiltrated files containing names and protected health information (PHI) from Radiology Associates of Richmond, impacting 266,000 patients in a breach with significant HIPAA regulatory implications.

biggest_hacks.title: DocketWise Data Breach Impacts 143,000
biggest_hacks.summary: Hackers accessed third-party partner repositories belonging to DocketWise, a legal immigration software platform, stealing names, addresses, Social Security numbers, financial information, and medical data for 143,000 individuals.

biggest_hacks.title: Oncology Institute Discloses Third-Party Data Breach
biggest_hacks.summary: The Oncology Institute has disclosed a data breach originating from a third-party vendor (possibly TriZetto), exposing patient data in yet another healthcare supply chain compromise with potential HIPAA liability.

vulnerabilities.description: Unauthenticated SQL injection in Ghost CMS Content API allows remote attackers to read arbitrary database content. Actively exploited at mass scale to inject ClickFix JavaScript payloads into 700+ compromised websites.

Hard-coded ASP.NET machine keys in KnowledgeDeliver LMS allow attackers to forge malicious ViewState payloads, achieving unauthenticated remote code execution. Exploited as a zero-day to deploy Godzilla web shell and Cobalt Strike Beacon.

Eight Packagist PHP packages were backdoored to download and execute a malicious Linux binary hosted on GitHub Releases. Affects any environment that installed affected package versions; exploitation is automatic on package install.

Malicious version tags published to Laravel-Lang repositories introduce backdoors that exfiltrate CI/CD secrets and deploy cross-platform credential-stealing malware. Exploitation is automatic for any project that resolved affected tag versions.

The Kali365 PhaaS platform abuses the legitimate OAuth device code authentication flow to steal M365 session tokens and bypass MFA — not a software vulnerability per se, but a protocol-level abuse actively exploited against business tenants with FBI warning issued.

Known issue introduced by the KB5087537 May 2026 security update causes domain controller lookup failures on Windows Server 2016 systems, potentially disrupting Active Directory authentication in affected environments.
